title: Get started with annotatR
text: package bundles three small example assets, reachable at_example_image(): "tissue" RGB raster, four-channel "multiplex" pyramid, 40-band spectral "cube". use tissue image throughout. annot_image thin, lazy handle pluggable backend rather pixels . handful accessors tell working : ordinary 512 512 RGB image three bands spectral axis. multiplex cube image report several bands, wavelengths , often, multiple pyramid levels; accessors regardless, lets one annotation workflow span different data. Coordinates follow image convention used everywhere annotatR: origin sits top-left corner, y increases downward, pixel (, j) centre (j - 0.5, - 0.5). title: The annotation model
text: Annotations built four nested classes: annot_roi -> annot_layer -> annot_project -> annot_session. annot_roi single region interest: sf geometry (point, polygon, ellipse, ) stored pixel coordinates declared pyramid level, together label, unique identifier, provenance. annot_layer groups ROIs share controlled label vocabulary drawing style. Layers unit visibility, locking, z-order. Adding ROI never mutates input; returns extended copy. annot_project binds one image named set layers records provenance. object query, validate, rasterise, export. at_rois() returns tidy table coordinates, areas, centroids expressed level 0, level column preserves ROI originally defined. Finally, annot_session wraps queue images manifest, cursor, shared label layer templates, project can materialised, annotated, saved image turn.
code: rect <- at_roi_rect(120, 150, 260, 290, label = "tumour") rect #> <annot_roi> tumour (POLYGON) #> id: "roi_000000002"  |  level: 0  |  source: manual #> bbox: [120, 150] - [260, 290] at_roi_area(rect) #> [1] 19600 regions <- at_layer("regions", labels = c("tumour", "stroma")) regions <- at_layer_add(regions, rect) regions <- at_layer_add(regions, at_roi_circle(400, 120, r = 40, label = "stroma")) regions #> <annot_layer> regions #> ROIs: 2  |  labels: "tumour" and "stroma" #> visible: TRUE  |  locked: FALSE  |  z: 1 img  <- at_example_image("tissue") proj <- at_project(img, regions, name = "demo") at_layers(proj) #> # A tibble: 1 × 6 #>   name    n_rois labels    visible locked     z #>   <chr>    <int> <list>    <lgl>   <lgl>  <int> #> 1 regions      2 <chr [2]> TRUE    FALSE      1 at_rois(proj)[, c("roi_id", "layer", "label", "geom_type", "level", "area_px")] #> # A tibble: 2 × 6 #>   roi_id        layer   label  geom_type level area_px #>   <chr>         <chr>   <chr>  <chr>     <int>   <dbl> #> 1 roi_000000002 regions tumour POLYGON       0  19600  #> 2 roi_000000003 regions stroma POLYGON       0   5018. sess <- at_example_session(3) at_session_status(sess)[, c("idx", "name", "status")] #> # A tibble: 3 × 3 #>     idx name     status  #>   <int> <chr>    <chr>   #> 1     1 image_01 pending #> 2     2 image_02 pending #> 3     3 image_03 pending

text: Every constructor finalises geometry: CRS cleared , result topologically invalid, sf::st_make_valid() applied warning. ROIs build R therefore valid construction. Geometry arrives elsewhere – imported GeoJSON, QuPath project, hand-edited file – carries guarantee, annotatR offers explicit audit. at_check_geometry() reports one row per problem across whole project: self-intersections, zero-area degenerate rings, duplicate vertices, reversed hole winding, NA coordinates, vertices outside image bounds, tagged severity whether can repaired automatically. add one ROI spills past image edge one duplicated vertex: at_fix_geometry() repairs can – duplicate vertices – reports rest. --bounds vertices boundary advisory rather topological fault, left untouched; clip at_clamp() want geometry confined image.
code: proj <- at_add_roi(proj, "regions", at_roi_rect(430, 430, 620, 620, label = "tumour")) dup  <- at_roi_polygon(   matrix(c(0, 0, 0, 0, 40, 0, 40, 40, 0, 40), ncol = 2, byrow = TRUE),   label = "stroma" ) proj <- at_add_roi(proj, "regions", dup) at_check_geometry(proj) #> # A tibble: 2 × 4 #>   roi_id        issue              severity fixable #>   <chr>         <chr>              <chr>    <lgl>   #> 1 roi_000000004 out_of_bounds      warning  TRUE    #> 2 roi_000000005 duplicate_vertices warning  TRUE proj <- at_fix_geometry(proj) #> ✔ Repaired 2 ROIs. at_check_geometry(proj) #> # A tibble: 0 × 4 #> # ℹ 4 variables: roi_id <chr>, issue <chr>, severity <chr>, fixable <lgl>

title: The annotation model
text: Whole-slide multiplex images pyramids: scene stored several resolutions. ROI records level coordinates digitised level field, region drawn low-resolution overview never silently misread full-resolution pixels. Keeping declared level makes every coordinate unambiguous every transform reversible. Two functions move coordinates levels. at_roi_rescale() assumes exact power--two pyramid needs image: going level 0 level 2 divides coordinates four. at_transform() instead uses real per-level dimensions image, exact pyramids downsampling ratio. bundled multiplex example, whose levels measure 512, 256, 128 pixels, two approaches agree: transforms exactly invertible, coordinates can round-trip level without drift. companion Masks vignette shows annotations rasterised – applying pixel-centre rule – binary, labelled, multi-class integer masks.
code: r0 <- at_roi_rect(0, 0, 100, 100, label = "a") r2 <- at_roi_rescale(r0, from_level = 0, to_level = 2) at_roi_bbox(r2) #> [1]  0  0 25 25 mimg <- at_example_image("multiplex") at_dims(mimg, level = 0) #> [1] 512 512 at_dims(mimg, level = 2) #> [1] 128 128 at_roi_bbox(at_transform(r0, from_level = 0, to_level = 2, img = mimg)) #> [1]  0  0 25 25

title: Images and backends
text: Whole-slide microscopy hyperspectral cubes routinely gigabytes size, annotatR never loads wholesale. Reading image returns annot_image: lightweight, backend-agnostic handle carries metadata need annotate — dimensions, pyramid levels, bands, pixel size — together lazy accessor fetches pixels asked. dim() handle c(width, height, bands). Printing summarises backend opened , data type, extent, nothing touched pixels . point: can inspect, transform plan annotations huge image modest machine, handle hundred bytes regardless large underlying file . handle also exposes accessors everything annotation workflow needs: at_n_bands() at_bands() channels, at_pixel_size() physical scale, at_meta() backend-specific keys source path data type. simply reads field handle — /O involved.
code: img <- at_example_image("tissue") img #> <annot_image> example_tissue.png #> backend: "raster"  |  dtype: "uint8" #> size: 512 x 512 px  |  levels: 1  |  bands: 3 #> pixel size: 1 x 1 px dim(img) #> [1] 512 512   3

title: Images and backends
text: Slide multiplex formats store scene several resolutions — pyramid. Level 0 full resolution; higher level coarser overview. multiplex example three-level pyramidal TIFF. Levels matter two reasons. First, overview lets display navigate whole image without reading full resolution. Second, ROI drawn coarse level records level created , coordinates can rescaled exactly level 0 (see at_roi_rescale() at_transform()). Every geometry annotatR anchored pyramid level; coordinate convention image pixels origin top-left y increasing downward.
code: mx <- at_example_image("multiplex") at_n_levels(mx) #> [1] 3 at_is_pyramidal(mx) #> [1] TRUE  levels <- 0:(at_n_levels(mx) - 1L) data.frame(   level  = levels,   width  = vapply(levels, function(l) at_dims(mx, l)[1], integer(1)),   height = vapply(levels, function(l) at_dims(mx, l)[2], integer(1)) ) #>   level width height #> 1     0   512    512 #> 2     1   256    256 #> 3     2   128    128

title: Images and backends

title: Images and backends
text: Whatever backend, pixels come one function, at_tile(), always three-dimensional [y, x, band] numeric array — even single band. choose pyramid level, optional pixel window, optional subset bands. request scoped, 64x64x4 block read. display cheap thumbnail whole image, read coarsest level full: Spectral cubes handled accessor; band metadata simply carries wavelengths, can read back image accessors.
code: tile <- at_tile(mx, level = 0, xrange = c(1, 64), yrange = c(1, 64)) dim(tile) #> [1] 64 64  4 overview <- at_tile(mx, level = 2) dim(overview) #> [1] 128 128   4  dim(at_tile(mx, level = 2, bands = 1)) #> [1] 128 128   1 cu <- at_example_image("cube") at_is_spectral(cu) #> [1] TRUE head(at_bands(cu), 3) #> # A tibble: 3 × 4 #>   index name   wavelength unit       #>   <int> <chr>       <dbl> <chr>      #> 1     1 Band 1       450  Nanometers #> 2     2 Band 2       462. Nanometers #> 3     3 Band 3       473. Nanometers range(at_wavelengths(cu)) #> [1] 450 900

title: Images and backends
text: Adding support new format means supplying four functions calling at_backend_register(). read_fn returns annot_image — classed list metadata plus handle accessor — tile_fn turns request [y, x, band] array. complete, self-contained backend toy “constant image” format stores size fill value, synthesises pixels demand. new backend now behaves like — appears registry, auto-detected file, serves tiles at_tile().
code: const_read <- function(path, ...) {   spec <- readRDS(path)                 # list(width, height, bands, value)   structure(     list(       source     = path,       backend    = "const",       dims       = c(spec$width, spec$height),       n_levels   = 1L,       level_dims = list(c(spec$width, spec$height)),       n_bands    = spec$bands,       band_names = paste0("Band ", seq_len(spec$bands)),       pixel_size = c(1, 1),       pixel_unit = "px",       dtype      = "double",       handle     = list(value = spec$value),   # no pixels, just the fill value       meta       = list()     ),     class = "annot_image"   ) }  const_tile <- function(img, level, xrange, yrange, bands) {   nx <- xrange[2] - xrange[1] + 1L   ny <- yrange[2] - yrange[1] + 1L   nb <- if (is.null(bands)) img$n_bands else length(bands)   array(img$handle$value, dim = c(ny, nx, nb)) }  at_backend_register(   name         = "const",   read_fn      = const_read,   tile_fn      = const_tile,   detect_fn    = function(path) grepl("\\.const$", path, ignore.case = TRUE),   available_fn = function() TRUE,   description  = "Constant-value demo backend",   extensions   = "const" ) path <- tempfile(fileext = ".const") saveRDS(list(width = 64L, height = 48L, bands = 2L, value = 0.5), path)  cimg <- at_read_image(path) cimg #> <annot_image> file2d441be5e22b.const #> backend: "const"  |  dtype: "double" #> size: 64 x 48 px  |  levels: 1  |  bands: 2 #> pixel size: 1 x 1 px dim(at_tile(cimg, xrange = c(1, 8), yrange = c(1, 8))) #> [1] 8 8 2

title: Interoperability
text: at_write_geojson() serialises project standard FeatureCollection. ROI becomes one Feature whose geometry pixel-coordinate polygon whose properties carry full annotatR schema: roi_id, layer, label, level, author, created, modified, source, writing annotatR_version, free-form attributes. Keeping schema explicit lets file survive return trip. roi_id preserved verbatim, ROI keeps identity across boundary can join exported measurements back original annotation. Reading file back at_read_geojson() reconstructs one annot_layer per distinct layer property. rebuild project original image check labels came intact.
code: gj <- tempfile(fileext = ".geojson") at_write_geojson(proj, gj) cat(readLines(gj)[1:22], sep = "\n") #> { #>   "type": "FeatureCollection", #>   "features": [ #>     { #>       "type": "Feature", #>       "id": "roi_000000001", #>       "geometry": { #>         "type": "Polygon", #>         "coordinates": [ #>           [ #>             [120, 150], #>             [260, 150], #>             [260, 290], #>             [120, 290], #>             [120, 150] #>           ] #>         ] #>       }, #>       "properties": { #>         "roi_id": "roi_000000001", #>         "layer": "regions", #>         "label": "tumour", back <- at_read_geojson(gj) imported <- at_project(proj$image, back[["regions"]]) identical(sort(at_rois(proj)$label), sort(at_rois(imported)$label)) #> [1] TRUE

title: Interoperability
text: annotatR’s convention image orientation: origin top-left y increases downward. Many GIS tools instead expect y increase upward. Set flip_y = TRUE write coordinates upward convention; y-axis mirrored image height. write flipped, must read flipped, supplying height inversion undone: Leave flip_y default FALSE exchanging image-coordinate tools (including QuPath annotatR ); reach downstream consumer explicitly wants cartesian, bottom-left origin.
code: h <- at_dims(proj$image)[2] gj_flip <- tempfile(fileext = ".geojson") at_write_geojson(proj, gj_flip, flip_y = TRUE) regained <- at_read_geojson(gj_flip, flip_y = TRUE, height = h) identical(sort(at_rois(at_project(proj$image, regained[["regions"]]))$centroid_y),           sort(at_rois(proj)$centroid_y)) #> [1] TRUE

title: Interoperability
text: QuPath stores classification colour signed 32-bit integer packed 0xFFRRGGBB. 0xFF alpha byte pushes colours past 2^31, wrap around negative values: grey #999999 serialises -6710887, friendly positive number. annotatR handles modular arithmetic directions, never touch raw integer, worth knowing field looks odd. Reading file back recovers hex colours onto layer style:
code: lyr <- at_read_qupath(qp) lyr$style$colour #>    tumour  necrosis    stroma  #> "#999999" "#E69F00" "#56B4E9"

title: Interoperability
text: pixel-level pipelines exchange currency raster mask, polygon. at_write_mask() writes integer TIFF alongside self-describing <path>.legend.json sidecar records mask type, level, dimensions, one entry per class (value, label, layer, roi_id, n_px, colour). sidecar turns anonymous grid integers something downstream model can interpret without guessing value meant class, travels raster mapping never lost. used "labelled" mask, ROI gets integer; "binary" mask collapses everything foreground background, "multiclass" mask shares one integer per label. Whichever choose, legend describes exactly pixels mean. Python side, read TIFF integer array load legend map values back labels. chunk illustrative run vignette built.
code: m <- at_mask(proj, type = "labelled") mp <- tempfile(fileext = ".tiff") at_write_mask(m, mp) cat(readLines(paste0(mp, ".legend.json"))[1:14], sep = "\n") #> { #>   "annotatR_version": "0.0.1", #>   "created": "2026-07-21T12:35:22+0000", #>   "mask_type": "labelled", #>   "level": 0, #>   "dims": [512, 512], #>   "source_project": "example", #>   "legend": [ #>     { #>       "value": 1, #>       "label": "tumour", #>       "layer": "regions", #>       "roi_id": "roi_000000001", #>       "n_px": 19600, import json import numpy as np import tifffile  mask = tifffile.imread("mask.tiff") with open("mask.tiff.legend.json") as f:     legend = json.load(f)  labels = {e["value"]: e["label"] for e in legend["legend"]} for value, label in labels.items():     print(label, int(np.sum(mask == value)), "px")

title: Masks
text: at_mask() writes one three rasters, chosen type: "binary" — logical matrix: TRUE wherever region covers pixel, FALSE elsewhere. Use foreground/background problems (“pixel annotated ?”). "labelled" — one distinct positive integer per ROI, assigned draw order. Use individual objects must stay separable, e.g. instance segmentation two adjacent tumour nests different things. "multiclass" — one integer per label class, every ROI sharing label collapses value. Use semantic segmentation, care class (“tumour”, “stroma”) particular ROI. Every mask annot_mask: matrix attached legend tibble (value, label, layer, roi_id, n_px, colour) plus level, dims, mask_type attributes. Read legend back at_mask_legend().

title: Masks
text: Rasterisation reproducible pixel/geometry relationship exact, annotatR pins . Pixel (, j) covers half-open square [j-1, j) x [-1, ), (0, 0) top-left corner top-left pixel; centre therefore (j - 0.5, - 0.5). default touches = FALSE, pixel mask centre lies inside polygon, using half-open [lower, upper) tie rule: centre lower edge counts inside, one upper edge outside. cleanest way trust compute small case eye. Take rectangle (2, 2) (5, 5) 10x10 grid: Rows columns 3, 4 5 set, nothing else. rectangle spans x [2, 5); pixel-centre x-coordinates fall interval 2.5, 3.5, 4.5, .e. columns 3, 4, 5. centre x = 5.5 (column 6) outside, lower edge x = 2 inside centre 2.5 > 2. reasoning y gives rows 3:5. four-pixel-wide rectangle covers exactly nine pixels — fencepost surprises.

title: Masks
text: touches = TRUE switches “polygon touch pixel ” rule (GDAL ALL_TOUCHED=TRUE), grows region fringe pixels polygon merely clips. matters edges cut pixel interiors rather running along grid. rectangle fractional bounds shows contrast: touches = FALSE pixels whose centres sit inside rectangle kept; touches = TRUE partially clipped border pixels join . Prefer default area-faithful masks, touches = TRUE must drop thin structures.

title: Masks
text: two regions cover pixel, overlap decides wins. ROIs rasterised draw order (ascending z, insertion): "last" (default) lets later-drawn region overwrite; "first" keeps earlier one; "max" "min" resolve pixel value; "error" aborts moment two regions collide, safest choice overlaps never happen.

what: Writing masks and the legend sidecar
title: Masks
text: at_write_mask() writes integer TIFF (16-bit default), — bare integer raster meaningless without key — companion <path>.legend.json describing : schema self-describing: annotatR_version, created timestamp, mask_type, pyramid level, raster dims, source_project, full legend array (one object per value, mirroring legend tibble). consumer can map pixel values back labels without touching R.
code: dir  <- tempfile("masks-"); dir.create(dir) path <- file.path(dir, "regions.tif") at_write_mask(mc, path, overwrite = TRUE) list.files(dir) #> [1] "regions.tif"             "regions.tif.legend.json" cat(readLines(paste0(path, ".legend.json")), sep = "\n") #> { #>   "annotatR_version": "0.0.1", #>   "created": "2026-07-21T12:35:25+0000", #>   "mask_type": "multiclass", #>   "level": 0, #>   "dims": [512, 512], #>   "source_project": "example", #>   "legend": [ #>     { #>       "value": 1, #>       "label": "tumour", #>       "layer": "regions", #>       "roi_id": null, #>       "n_px": 19600, #>       "colour": "#999999" #>     }, #>     { #>       "value": 2, #>       "label": "necrosis", #>       "layer": "regions", #>       "roi_id": null, #>       "n_px": 72704, #>       "colour": "#E69F00" #>     }, #>     { #>       "value": 3, #>       "label": "stroma", #>       "layer": "regions", #>       "roi_id": null, #>       "n_px": 34200, #>       "colour": "#56B4E9" #>     } #>   ] #> }

title: Masks
text: Python pipeline reads TIFF legend directly — R runtime, bespoke format:
code: import json import tifffile  mask = tifffile.imread("regions.tif")            # integer array, image grid with open("regions.tif.legend.json") as f:     legend = json.load(f)  value_to_label = {row["value"]: row["label"] for row in legend["legend"]} tumour = mask == next(v for v, l in value_to_label.items() if l == "tumour")

title: Check cross-layer containment — at_check_containment
text: Report ROIs constrained layer fall outside container region. layer declares constraint metadata, e.g. at_layer("state", within = list(layer = "anatomy", label = "wound")); every ROI state must spatially covered union anatomy layer's wound ROIs. enforces annotation rule class painted inside region interest. report mirrors shape at_check_geometry().

title: Check cross-layer containment — at_check_containment
text: project annot_project. tol Non-negative slack, level-0 pixels, container grown testing, tolerate sub-pixel tracing overhang. Default 0. call calling environment, error reporting.

title: Check cross-layer containment — at_check_containment
text: tibble::tibble columns roi_id, layer, issue, severity ("warning" ROI outside container, "error" missing/empty container), fixable (always FALSE). 0-row tibble every constrained ROI contained, layer declares within constraint.

title: Check cross-layer containment — at_check_containment
code: anatomy <- at_layer_add(at_layer("anatomy", labels = "wound"),                         at_roi_rect(2, 2, 8, 8, label = "wound")) state <- at_layer("state", labels = "injury",                   within = list(layer = "anatomy", label = "wound")) state <- at_layer_add(state, at_roi_rect(0, 0, 4, 4, label = "injury")) at_check_containment(at_project(at_example_image("cube"), list(anatomy, state))) #> # A tibble: 1 × 5 #>   roi_id        layer issue                                     severity fixable #>   <chr>         <chr> <chr>                                     <chr>    <lgl>   #> 1 roi_000000002 state ROI is not contained in layer 'anatomy' … warning  FALSE

code: at_mask(   x,   type = c("binary", "labelled", "multiclass"),   layer = NULL,   label = NULL,   level = 0L,   background = 0L,   touches = FALSE,   dims = NULL,   values = NULL,   overlap = c("last", "first", "max", "min", "error", "bitor"),   engine = c("stars", "terra"),   call = rlang::caller_env() )

title: Rasterise ROIs to a mask (
text: x annot_roi, annot_layer, annot_project. type "binary" (logical matrix), "labelled" (one integer id per ROI), "multiclass" (one id per label class). layer Optional layer name(s) restrict (projects ). label Optional label(s) restrict . level Integer pyramid level rasterise. Default 0. background Integer background value. Default 0. touches Logical; see coverage contract. Default FALSE. dims Optional c(width, height); taken image (projects) geometry bounding box otherwise. values Optional named integer vector mapping labels explicit class codes (e.g. c(specular = 1L, blood = 2L, shadow = 4L)), used type = "multiclass". NULL (default) codes follow first-seen label order. Supply power--two codes together overlap = "bitor" build bitfield mask. overlap overlapping ROIs resolve: "last" (later z-order wins, default), "first", "max", "min", "error" (abort overlap), "bitor" (bitwise-overlapping values, bitfield masks; use power--two values background = 0). engine "stars" (reference) "terra" (accelerated, installed); two produce identical masks. call calling environment, error reporting.

title: annotatR 0.0.1
text: Initial development release.

title: annotatR 0.0.1
text: at_read_image() reads image lightweight annot_image handle, auto-detecting backend. at_tile() universal [y, x, band] tile accessor. Six backends ship (raster, tiff, ometiff, cuvis, tivita, envi); register at_backend_register(). tivita backend reads bare Diaspective Vision TIVITA *_SpecCube.dat cubes directly (big-endian float32, 640x480x100, 500-995 nm), addition ENVI-conformant exports; cubes also auto-detect. Accessors: at_dims(), at_n_levels(), at_n_bands(), at_bands(), at_wavelengths(), at_is_spectral(), at_is_pyramidal(), at_pixel_size(), at_meta().

title: annotatR 0.0.1

text: at_mask() produces binary, labelled, multi-class integer masks documented pixel-coverage contract, six overlap policies, self-describing legend. values argument pins labels explicit integer codes, "bitor" overlap policy bitwise-ORs overlapping values build bitfield masks (e.g. artefact layer pixel specular | blood).
